rows.title: U.S. Airlines Add Flights As Demand Increases, But Recovery Will Take Years
rows.standfirst: Ahead of the summer travel season, several U.S. airlines are expanding their flight schedules. But a complete recovery from the economic fallout caused by the coronavirus pandemic could take years.

rows.title: TikTok Pivots From Dance Moves To A Racial Justice Movement
rows.standfirst: TikTok has become the go-to platform for youth activism over George Floyd's death and Black Lives Matter. It follows an apology from the Chinese-owned app for hiding videos related to the protests.

rows.title: Facebook Will Review Policies On Posts About State Violence, Voting
rows.standfirst: Mark Zuckerberg says the company will consider labeling some posts that break its rules, as Twitter has done with the president's inflammatory and false tweets.

rows.title: Police Unions And Police Violence
rows.standfirst: We look at the data connecting police unions and police violence. Today's episode comes from our daily podcast, The Indicator. Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: Caravan For Justice: Cars Offer Socially Distanced Protesting During Pandemic
rows.standfirst: Hundreds of cars circle San Francisco, festooned with signs honoring George Floyd and other black victims of police violence. Similar protests are planned from Detroit to Connecticut.

rows.title: Debate Over Racial Justice Coverage Roils 'N.Y. Times,' 'Philadelphia Inquirer'
rows.standfirst: After reporters publicly rebelled, leaders at The New York Times and The Philadelphia Inquirer apologize for publishing controversial pieces on law enforcement and the protests over racial injustice.

rows.title: New Job Report Shows Signs Of Improving Economy
rows.standfirst: A monthly job report published Friday has shown signs of strength in the labor market. Unemployment has declined and employers have created millions of new jobs in May.

rows.title: Unemployment And The Racial Divide
rows.standfirst: How well a family can endure a spell of unemployment depends on how much of a buffer it has to fall back on. And there are big racial and ethnic disparities in how big those buffers are.

rows.title: Trump Says Strong Economy Will Bring Racial Justice
rows.standfirst: The president intimates that George Floyd, killed by police, would be happy with the lower than expected unemployment rate.

rows.title: LinkedIn CEO Condemns Employees' 'Appalling Comments' On Race
rows.standfirst: During an all-staff meeting, anonymous employees deride the racial justice protests and question the professional networking company's diversity initiatives.

rows.title: For Bangladesh's Struggling Garment Workers, Hunger Is A Bigger Worry Than Pandemic
rows.standfirst: Many garment factories have reopened, but the coronavirus still affects global demand and orders remain canceled. "I need to work," says one employee. "I'll die of hunger before I die of this virus."

rows.title: COVID-19 Outbreak In Pacific Northwest Seafood Industry As Season Ramps Up
rows.standfirst: Most of the crew on one massive seafood trawler has tested positive for COVID-19. Other vessels also have cases, despite sweeping measures to try and prevent the spread of coronavirus.

rows.title: May Surprise: U.S. Adds 2.5 Million Jobs As Unemployment Dips To 13.3%
rows.standfirst: U.S. employers unexpectedly added jobs last month as the unemployment rate declined, signs that people are returning to work as states reopen their economies. President Trump celebrated the news.

rows.title: Farmers Find Ways To Save Millions Of Pigs From Being Euthanized
rows.standfirst: When COVID-19 infections forced pork companies to close processing plants, some farmers predicted that it would force them to euthanize millions of hogs. The actual number has been much lower.

rows.title: Facebook Begins Labeling 'State-Controlled' Media
rows.standfirst: The social network is flagging publishers it says are under 'editorial control' of governments, as part of efforts to secure its platform against foreign influence campaigns.

rows.title: Supermarket Prices Still Climbing Amid Coronavirus Pandemic
rows.standfirst: Even as restaurants start to re-open, analysts say we're likely to keep eating more of our meals at home for some time to come, which is affecting grocery prices.

rows.title: Patent Racism
rows.standfirst: Violence, including racist attacks, stifles innovation and the economy. Dr. Lisa Cook proved how. It took 10 years to be heard. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: The Business Of Police Surveillance
rows.standfirst: The companies that lead the field in surveillance technology are turning against it.

rows.title: Walmart, CVS, Walgreens To End Practice Of Locking Up Black Beauty Products
rows.standfirst: Three major chains share their decisions in separate statements, bowing to what Walmart called "concerns raised by our customers and members of the community."

rows.title: Homelessness In Los Angeles County Rises Sharply
rows.standfirst: Los Angeles County's annual homeless count came out Friday and shows a double-digit increase over last year. The pandemic is also causing future homelessness projections to skyrocket.

rows.title: World Bank: Recession Is The Deepest In Decades
rows.standfirst: The World Bank issues a report this week detailing the extent of the recession, the first caused solely by a pandemic. Its findings are sobering — but do offer a glimmer of hope.

rows.title: Dow Gains 477 Points After Dramatic Plunge Spurred By A Spike In Coronavirus Cases
rows.standfirst: Major stock indexes bounce back a day after the Dow lost 1,861 points amid spikes in new cases in states that had reopened their economies.

rows.title: Dear Class Of 2020: Graduation Messages From Front-Line Workers
rows.standfirst: NPR asked essential workers — who normally would not be asked speak at a commencement ceremony — to offer insight forged by the simple act of showing up every day and doing what needs to be done.

rows.title: EPA Orders Amazon And EBay To Stop Selling Bogus Coronavirus-Fighting Products
rows.standfirst: On Thursday the EPA ordered the e-commerce giants to stop selling a list of unregistered and misbranded products, some of which contained toxic chemicals like methylene chloride and chlorine dioxide.

rows.title: Story Of A Paper
rows.standfirst: Why a groundbreaking paper by Lisa Cook on the effects of racist violence took ten years to get published.

rows.title: Biden Warns Facebook On Track To Repeat Mistakes Of 2016 Election
rows.standfirst: The presumptive Democratic presidential nominee demands the social network fact-check ads from political candidates, saying its hands-off policies "pose a threat to free and fair elections."

rows.title: Biden Outlines Plan To Restart Economy, Including Testing Every Worker
rows.standfirst: The presumptive Democratic nominee spoke with Philadelphia community leaders about protecting public health while reopening businesses and schools, aided by expansive federal involvement and spending.

rows.title: Critics Slam Facebook But Zuckerberg Resists Blocking Trump's Posts
rows.standfirst: People inside and outside Facebook are furious over the social network's refusal to curb President Trump's most inflammatory messages. The concerns reflect long-running frustrations with the company.

rows.title: Market Meltdown: Dow Dives 1,800 Points On Worries Of 2nd Coronavirus Wave
rows.standfirst: The Dow and other stock indexes plunged as cases surged in several states and the Federal Reserve warned that the pandemic "will weigh heavily on economic activity."

rows.title: Another 1.5 Million File For Unemployment As States Continue To Reopen Economies
rows.standfirst: The pain in the job market continues as an additional 1.5 million sought unemployment benefits last week. In the past 12 weeks, more than 44 million new claims have been filed.

rows.title: Tips For Creating Equity For Transgender People At Your Workplace
rows.standfirst: NPR's Life Kit provides tips on how to make your workplace more equitable for transgender people.

rows.title: China Suspends Poultry Imports From Tyson Foods Plant In Arkansas
rows.standfirst: The country's customs office said shipments from the plant would be temporarily suspended, while products that have already arrived will be seized.

rows.title: The Latest Pandemic Shortage: Coins Are The New Toilet Paper
rows.standfirst: In another sign of how the coronavirus crisis is disrupting commerce, banks are running short of nickels, dimes and quarters. The Federal Reserve, which supplies banks, is having to ration change.

rows.title: Trump Freezes Green Cards, Many Work Visas Until End Of Year
rows.standfirst: The White House says pausing immigration and a variety of temporary work visas will help respond to job losses caused by the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Money And Justice
rows.standfirst: Money and social change. We talk policing, nonprofits, reparations, and the awkwardness of brands getting woke. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: AMC Theatres Will Now Require Guests To Wear Masks When It Reopens
rows.standfirst: After an outcry, the multiplex chain said it will require face coverings for guests in all of its theaters reopening in July. Earlier plans mandated masks only for staff and where laws required them.

rows.title: Apple Closing 11 Stores Again In States Seeing a Spike in Coronavirus Cases
rows.standfirst: Stores in Florida, North Carolina, South Carolina and Arizona are once again shutting their doors, beginning Saturday, as those states see mounting coronavirus cases and hospitalizations.

rows.title: Big Talk From Big Tech On Racial Equity, But Not All Workers Are Buying It
rows.standfirst: More than 200 technology companies have issued statements supporting the advancement of racial justice, but Black tech workers say internal policies and tech culture needs an overhaul first.

rows.title: Facebook And Twitter Remove 'Racist Baby' Video Posted By President Trump
rows.standfirst: The video, which condemns "fake news," fabricates a supposed-CNN segment from last year. The social media companies said the footage violated copyright rules.

rows.title: Daymond John: Swimming With Sharks
rows.standfirst: Daymond John, founder of the iconic brand FUBU and investor on the reality show Shark Tank, talked to us about how he got his start and maintained his lead in the cutthroat world of fashion apparel.

rows.title: 'New York Times', 'Washington Post' Promise Major Changes To Move Forward On Race
rows.standfirst: The Post announces more than a dozen new jobs involving race and the Times says it will devise a strategy to better hire, develop, support and promote people, particularly people of color.

rows.title: Restaurants Are Closing. Again.
rows.standfirst: The Supreme Court ruled Thursday that the Trump administration's plan to end DACA — Deferred Action For Childhood Arrivals — was "arbitrary and capricious." The ruling is welcome news for recipients of the program, some of whom are essential workers on the front lines of the fight against COVID-19.

rows.title: When A Boomtown Goes Bust
rows.standfirst: Williston, North Dakota doubled in size during the shale oil boom a decade ago. Now oil prices have fallen and the town's facing hard times.

rows.title: Two U.K. Companies Apologize, Pledge Donations Over Slavery Legacies
rows.standfirst: Lloyd's of London and pub chain Greene King said they'd donate to charities helping minority communities. A research project documented that founders of the companies received money linked to slavery.

rows.title: 1.5 Million File For Unemployment, But Continuing Claims Decrease Slightly
rows.standfirst: Another 1.5 million people file for unemployment benefits for the first time, but the number who are continuing to seek the payments continues to decline as workers return to their jobs.

rows.title: Airbus Announces Job Cuts Amid Massive Dip In Aircraft Orders
rows.standfirst: The European passenger-jet maker says it plans to cut 15,000 jobs amid a 40% drop in its business since the start of the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Listener Questions: Past Pandemics And Property Prices
rows.standfirst: On the Spanish Flu, housing prices, and the resilience of Australia's economy. Indicator listener questions, answered.

rows.title: Economy Of The Berkshires In Western Massachusetts Suffers From Arts Cancellations
rows.standfirst: The Tanglewood Music Festival and Massachusetts Museum of Contemporary Art bring the Berkshires of Western Massachusetts up to $150 million every year. But this year both of them are closed.

rows.title: Is Remote Work Here To Stay?
rows.standfirst: A new study shows that about half of the entire workforce is now remote. The case for why "this portends a much bigger shift in the economy."

rows.title: FAA Begins Test Flights For Boeing's Troubled 737 Max
rows.standfirst: More than a year after the plane's grounding because of two deadly crashes, the FAA began a series of certification flights Monday, a big step toward allowing the 737 Max to fly passengers again.

rows.title: Why writing a will and planning for your death is a 'lifetime gift' to loved ones
rows.standfirst: Talking about death makes many of us uncomfortable, so we don't plan for it. But the reality is that even a small amount of planning ensures our final wishes are honored — and makes it easier on our family and friends. This episode will help you get started on making a will and an advance directive, even if you don't have a big estate.

rows.title: Remdesivir Priced At More Than $3,100 For A Course Of Treatment
rows.standfirst: An experimental COVID-19 medicine that has been shown to shorten the time people with severe illness have to stay in the hospital finally has a price tag that's lower than some analysts expected.

rows.title: Reddit Bans The_Donald, Forum Of Nearly 800,000 Trump Fans, Over Abusive Posts
rows.standfirst: Reddit unveiled an update to its hate speech policies on Monday, including shutting down about 2,000 subreddits. It is the latest example of a popular online platform cracking down on hate speech.

rows.title: The Uncounted Workforce
rows.standfirst: Incarcerated Americans make goods for American companies, and get paid next to nothing for their labor.

rows.title: Facebook Boycott Grows: Ford Joins Coca-Cola, Starbucks And Other Brands
rows.standfirst: The list of major advertisers pulling out of Facebook continues to grow as the company weathers criticism over its handling of racist, violent and other hateful rhetoric on the platform.

rows.title: Supreme Court Gives President Power To Fire Key Independent Agency Chief
rows.standfirst: But the court left intact the rest of the statute that created the CFPB. The decision was a victory for President Trump and others who have long sought to trim the sails of independent agencies.

rows.title: How Coronavirus Could Widen The Gender Wage Gap
rows.standfirst: Women have slowly made economic gains over the last half-century, and the gender wage gap is as narrow as it has ever been. But coronavirus could reverse those gains, and motherhood is a big reason.

rows.title: In Colombia, Tax-Free Holidays Lead Critics To Decry 'COVID Friday'
rows.standfirst: Seeking ways to boost to its economy, Colombia has set aside three tax-free shopping days this summer. Critics fear they could become super spreader events for the coronavirus.

rows.title: Seed Spy
rows.standfirst: Espionage. Deceit. Theft. In this episode we follow the case of a global effort to steal top secret high technology: seeds. | Subscribe to our weekly newsletter here.

rows.title: How Much Have Facebook And Twitter Changed Since 2016?
rows.standfirst: How much has Big Tech changed since the 2016 election? Sam is joined by Washington Post tech reporters Elizabeth Dwoskin and Tony Romm. They chat about Facebook and Twitter and how their platforms and views on free speech have evolved since the last presidential election. Sam also chats with Washington Post columnist and satirist Alexandra Petri about her book of essays Nothing Is Wrong and Here Is Why and how she uses humor to uncover bigger truths.
